headline: Lilly's 18-yard overtime dash lifts Miami past USC 34-28
dek: Miami snaps an 0-2 start and climbs to 1-2 while USC drops its first game and falls to 2-1 in the Western Pacific race.
body: Overtime, 7:25 on the clock, third-and-8 at the USC 18: Graham Mertz handed to Colby Lilly, who burst through the left side and raced 18 yards for the winning touchdown, making it Miami 34, USC 28 and ending a seesaw night that had already produced four fourth-quarter lead changes.

Miami struck first at 10:42 of the second quarter when Mertz hit Ernie Simmons on a 9-yard score and the two-point conversion made it 8-0. USC answered twice before halftime — Miller Moss to Connor Burnett from 13 yards, then Moss to Patrick Farthing from 8 yards — to take a 14-8 lead. Vencie Sites' 24-yard field goal cut it to 14-11 at the break. Sites added a 44-yarder at 2:09 of the third to tie it at 14. USC surged ahead 21-14 on Raleigh Montgomery's 3-yard plunge at 9:59 of the fourth, but Romeo Dixon's 3-yard run at 6:42 knotted it again. Rodney Linville's 6-yard touchdown put USC up 28-21 at 4:02, only for Mertz to find Chimere Dike on a 12-yard strike with 41 seconds left to force overtime at 28-all.

The box score tells the story: Miami outgained USC 488-394, powered by Mertz's 41-of-67, 418-yard, two-touchdown effort that pushed his season total to 1,030 yards — second in the PCFL behind Tennessee's Geor MacIntyre (1,071). USC's Moss threw for 315 yards and two scores but the Trojans managed just 97 rushing yards on 32 carries, while Miami's ground game, though only 80 yards total, delivered the overtime winner. Third-down efficiency favored USC (60% to 50%), yet Miami converted all three fourth-down attempts and won the turnover battle when Jack Williams intercepted Moss at the Miami 31 on the first overtime possession. Lilly's 57 yards on five carries included the decisive 18-yarder; his season average now sits at 7.5 yards per carry, ninth in the league. USC's defense, allowing 430.3 yards per game (14th in the PCFL), couldn't contain Miami's 408 passing yards.

USC falls to 2-1 and slips from No. 2 to No. 6 in the power poll, now second in the Western Pacific behind Washington with a home date against the Huskies next week. Miami improves to 1-2, jumps from No. 14 to No. 9, and rides a one-game winning streak into a road trip to Georgia (0-3) looking to climb out of the Eastern Southern basement.
turningPoint: Overtime, 12:15 — Jack Williams intercepted Miller Moss at the Miami 31, giving the Hurricanes the ball and setting up the game-winning drive capped by Colby Lilly's 18-yard touchdown run at 7:25.
byTheNumbers: Miami 488 total yards vs. USC 394 — the Hurricanes' 408 passing yards overwhelmed a USC defense ranked 14th in the PCFL at 430.3 yards allowed per game.
Miami 3-for-3 on fourth down vs. USC 0-for-0 — every fourth-down conversion extended drives that produced points, including the overtime possession.
Zero Miami turnovers vs. one USC interception — Jack Williams' pick in overtime flipped the field and ended USC's opening overtime drive.
Colby Lilly 5 carries, 57 yards, 1 TD (18-yard overtime winner) — his 7.5 yards-per-carry season average ranks ninth in the PCFL.

unsungHero.name: Vencie Sites
unsungHero.why: Made both field-goal attempts (24 and 44 yards) and the game-tying extra point after the fourth-quarter touchdown, providing the only points of the first half for Miami and keeping the Hurricanes within striking distance.
